findings.title: Second `self.downsize` silently replaces the first, changing its arity
findings.body: The PR adds `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` while the existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (line 145) is still present. In Ruby the later definition wins, so the 5-argument form is dead code and any caller passing `(from, to, w, h, opts)` now has `h` bound to `opts`. Calling `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer raises or returns nil, so the call fails or silently ignores options. Duplicate method definitions with different signatures should not be merged like this. Either keep one signature or rename the new one.

findings.title: Removed `OptimizedImage.dimensions` helper and changed `optimize` signature
findings.body: The helper `self.dimensions(width, height)` is removed and `optimize` now takes a preformatted dimensions string instead of width and height. Any other caller in the codebase or plugins that calls `OptimizedImage.dimensions` or `optimize` with width/height will break with NoMethodError or wrong argument handling. The diff does not show that these callers were checked.

findings.title: File size re-check may read a stale size and loop without effect
findings.body: `tempfile.size` on an open Tempfile reads the size through its open file descriptor. `OptimizedImage.downsize` runs `convert` writing to `tempfile.path`. If ImageMagick writes via a new inode (unlink and create, or rename), the Tempfile's open handle still points at the old contents, so `tempfile.size` never drops. The loop then runs all 5 attempts with no effect and the original oversized file is passed to `Upload.create_for`. Use `File.size(tempfile.path)` or reopen the file to get the real size.

findings.title: Downsize failures are ignored and the uploaded file is overwritten in place
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false on failure (`convert_with` swallows errors and logs), but the return value is discarded. The loop then retries up to 5 times on the same input, and a partially written or corrupted output is left at `tempfile.path` and uploaded. The original file is destroyed in place with no fallback. Check the return value, stop on failure, and either keep the original or reject the upload.

findings.title: Client-side size limit hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings
findings.body: The check previously used `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. It now always uses 10MB for images and attachments alike. Admins' `max_attachment_size_kb` and `max_image_size_kb` are ignored on the client, so the client may accept or reject files that the server would treat differently. The feature's purpose (accept large images and downsize them) is also undermined because the client still hard-blocks anything above 10MB.

findings.title: 413 error message reports hardcoded 10 MB regardless of configured limit
findings.body: The HTTP 413 handler now shows a 10 MB limit instead of the configured `max_image_size_kb`. The displayed limit is wrong whenever the admin has configured a different value, and the message misleads users about the actual cap.

findings.title: Remote URL downloads now capped at 10MB instead of the configured image limit
findings.body: The URL download limit changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes`. This is unrelated to downsizing, applies to all URL uploads, and ignores the admin setting. If the intent is to allow larger images, the download cap should be an explicit, documented decision rather than a silent change.

findings.title: Downsizing applies to non-image-type uploads and to unbounded input
findings.body: The condition checks `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` but the downsize step runs on any upload where the filename looks like an image, including SVG, which ImageMagick may rasterize, and `image_type` is not considered. There is no guard against a huge source file being fed into ImageMagick before size is checked, so the conversion cost is paid on arbitrary input size.

findings.title: Duplicate `downsize` definitions are confusing to maintainers
findings.body: Two `self.downsize` methods with different parameter lists appear in the same class, which hides which version is live. This ambiguity is what causes the arity bug above. Remove the unused variant.
